bib.title: Learning to Reason without External Rewards

read.skipped: References skimmed only; Appendix C model-completion transcripts skimmed (garbled code glyphs).

question: Can an LLM improve its reasoning by RL using only an intrinsic, self-generated signal (its own confidence), with no external verifier or gold labels?
hypothesis: Optimising the model's own confidence (self-certainty) should improve reasoning, because LLMs are less confident on hard problems and higher confidence correlates with correctness.
contributions: Introduce RLIF, RL from internal feedback with no external supervision or labels
Introduce INTUITOR, using self-certainty as the sole reward in GRPO
Show INTUITOR matches GRPO in-domain and generalises competitively or better out-of-domain, with emergent structured reasoning and instruction following

method.summary: INTUITOR replaces the verifiable reward in GRPO with self-certainty (average KL from uniform to the next-token distribution over the response), normalised within the group to give advantages. Trained on MATH or Codeforces prompts only, then evaluated on math, code, MMLU-Pro and AlpacaEval; compared with GRPO (gold answers) and GRPO-PV (plurality-vote pseudo-labels).
method.task: RL fine-tuning of LLMs for reasoning without external rewards

datasets.name: MATH (train split)
datasets.preprocessing: chat prompt; no gold answers used by INTUITOR

datasets.name: AlpacaEval 2.0
datasets.preprocessing: length-controlled win rate, judged by GPT-4.1

training.objective: GRPO with reward u_i = self-certainty(o_i|q), advantage = (u_i - mean)/std within group, clipped importance ratio eps 0.2, KL penalty beta to reference; online (reward from current policy)
training.regularisation: KL penalty beta 0.0005 (MATH 1.5B/3B), 0.01 (7B/14B, Codeforces) per Table 10

other.group_size: 7 (MATH 1.5B/3B); 14 (7B/14B and Codeforces); 16 per Sec B.2 for 7B/14B
other.text_vs_table_conflict: Sec 4 says default beta=0.005 and lr reduced from 3e-5 to 1e-5 for Code, Table 10 says beta 0.0005, lr 3e-6 (MATH) and 1e-6 (Code); Table 3 labels the default run KL0.005; Sec B.2 says 16 samples for 7B/14B vs Table 10 group size 14
other.GRPO_PV: plurality-vote answer used as proxy ground truth, following TTRL
other.larger_model_changes: simplified system prompt, lr 1e-6, more samples (Sec B.2)

inference.samples: 1 greedy completion per item; single training run per config (no seeds stated)
inference.prompting: chat-style system prompt requiring step-by-step reasoning and \boxed{} answer; MMLU-Pro uses its original format

eval.protocol: single run per configuration; no seeds or confidence intervals; Mann-Whitney U tests for self-certainty separation of correct vs incorrect answers (Fig 8)

limits: Models are small (1.5B-14B) and trained on small corpora (7,500 MATH problems, 3,200 Codeforces problems); authors say scale to hundreds of billions untested.
Single run per configuration, no seeds or error bars; several gaps (e.g. 0.612 vs 0.636) not tested for significance.

INTUITOR is slightly worse than GRPO in-domain on most rows; out-of-domain gain is on LCB/CRUX and not uniform (OLMo-2 shows no code gain, Qwen2.5-1.5B CRUX 0.296 < GRPO 0.328, MMLU-Pro 0.379 < GRPO 0.403 on 3B).
Offline self-certainty is exploited (~step 100); scaling likely needs periodic online updates.
Fails when the model lacks prior knowledge or chat alignment (Llama3.2-3B-Base stays near zero); noisy data can induce repetitive degeneration; more hyperparameter sensitive (lr 3e-6 on 7B degrades).
Larger models needed changed recipe (lr, prompt, sample count), described as an untuned first trial.
No theory for why self-certainty works; combining with gold rewards only lightly explored.
Hyperparameter values in Sec 4 text conflict with Table 10.
Qwen contamination possible; OLMo-2 experiment offered as partial answer.
